reason: A turns the request into a tight eight-step story at phone width: you draw your week (step 2), see your miss (my test guess: 1,884 MW/h), watch 'repeat last week' beat it at 1,561 with the Thu 5 p.m. +2,046 MW overshoot marked (step 4), then Chronos-2 at 980 MW with its 80% band holding 140/168 hours (step 5); your guess then reappears as a ring beside every method in 'One week is one draw' (step 6), which flags AutoARIMA's 0.58 -> 1.11 swing, before the six-series averages with the 0.101 lead marked 'not established' (step 7) and the by-series take-away. B has more depth: a slider plus drawing, a live score card, a clickable 11-method bar chart that redraws each forecast and band, a This week / Ontario / All 6 series toggle and a full heatmap, all with correct numbers. But on a phone B is a long scroll page with several layout faults: the first chart needs a sideways swipe and hides its y-axis, the section 3 forecast chart's axis text is about 5 px, the section 4 tick labels overlap, and the heatmap hides the USD/CAD and AI page-view columns its own text discusses. A gives the reader the feeling the request asked for, how hard the baseline is to beat and by how much the models improve, more cleanly. B states the numbers more completely.

A: The forecast week is squeezed into about 140 px of the chart in steps 3-5, so your guess, the actual line, the red miss lines and the copy overlap into a dense tangle.
Steps 6-8 show mostly unlabelled dots (only AutoARIMA's 0.58 -> 1.11 is annotated), so readers must estimate values such as the Ontario ~0.64-0.68 and the by-series gaps from the axis.
The five-item legend repeats on every step with most items greyed out, adding clutter under the narrative.
B: At 390 px the step 1 drawing chart overflows (760 px wide, opened scrolled right), so the y-axis in MW is hidden and the earlier week needs a sideways swipe; dragging outside the forecast panel selects the axis text instead of drawing.
The section 3 forecast-and-band chart has axis labels about 5 px high (unreadable), and the section 4 tick labels ('1.00 = copy last week', 0.5, 1.5) overlap.

The section 5 heatmap is clipped at phone width with no scroll cue: the USD/CAD and AI page-view columns that the text discusses are off-screen, and the row labels scroll away when you swipe; at a tie (slider unmoved) the score card says 'Last week beat you'.
